name: Gaddi
overview: Gaddi was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh and is notably recognized as one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is his primary biblical distinction, as recorded in Numbers 13:11. This service highlights his involvement in a critical moment of Israel's journey to the Promised Land.
namesAndTitles: The name Gaddi means 'of G-d' and is a proper name mentioned in Numbers 13:11. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that reflects a connection to the divine.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Gaddi was the son of Susi, as noted in Numbers 13:11. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gaddi's significance lies in his role as one of the twelve spies representing the tribe of Manasseh during the reconnaissance of Canaan. This mission was pivotal in Israel's history, as the spies' reports influenced the people's faith and obedience to God. Gaddi's inclusion among the spies underscores his trusted position within his tribe and the nation during this formative event.
